Mac coverage belongs to ordinary PR CI and the pre-publication Darwin producer.
The three protected Mac context names are Linux carriers of the consolidated
job's real outcome. `REQUIRED_CONTEXT: "false"` is private to that execution job;
required-context governance accepts it only with all three always-running Linux
carriers and their exact fail-closed result command.

Release-plz uses a personal token belonging to the same account a person uses.
Its PR author is therefore not an automation credential. The manager-approved
release-only identity is a same-repository head with the configured branch prefix,
combined with semantic version/changelog-only content. A prefix, title or bot
login alone grants no omission. Unknown PR input requires Mac coverage.

`github-workflows:test` resolves the actual YAML and uses the published Actions
expression evaluator. The external screencomp call is read from its digest-pinned
source snapshot; its dynamic architecture output comes from this checkout's
`screencomp.toml`. Unrecognized calls, outputs and runners are errors. New reusable
calls need an explicit resolution before their scheduling can be measured.

`just nx run github-workflows:budgets` records telemetry through the uncached test
and then judges the two registered bounds. The reporters only consume that data
and reject a stale source-tree digest; thresholds are excluded from the digest
and read only by onebudgetspec. Manual diagnostics default off and are excluded
from automatic lifecycle totals.

The Darwin builder invokes maturin once for each target, retaining the release
profile's stripping. Its wheel binary feeds both archive and npm payloads, with
all three hashes recorded in `binary.json`. The same job installs staged CLI and
SDK distributions under arm64 and x86 interpreters, with Rosetta enabled, before
any Darwin upload or registry publication. The host-native SDK packaging journey
runs these production builders/installers without publishing; declared Darwin
commands are contract evidence until a Mac runner executes them.
